text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a cluster of slow timeseries renders in the canary this morning after the telemetry batcher change. Charts are stalling ~600-900ms on first paint. Data: http://perf.internal/rd/174800 (short link)
jon: ugh. saw increased main-thread parse and a big spike in kvcache misses around the same timestamp. Any recent console canary rollouts?
sahil: telemetry batcher v2 rolled to canary @ 03:10 UTC — it changes how we compute cache keys (adds samplingGroupId) and switches to continuous batching.
alex: can you paste the kvcache stats? miss rate, hit latency, eviction rate?
maria: here — kvcache summary (canary pool, last 30m): misses 92%, hits 8%, avg_hop_latency 18ms, evictions up 4x. Also 12% more module parse bytes on main thread.
samir: that samplingGroupId in the prefix would blow up cardinality. If keys are per-sample we lose prefix/KV reuse between similar requests.
jon: bingo. our cache was keyed by route+prefixHash previously. the patch adds `:${samplingGroupId}` — see snippet from the client change:

```
- const key = `${routeKey}:${prefixHash}`
+ const key = `${routeKey}:${prefixHash}:${samplingGroupId}`
```

alex: rough numbers: with added group id cardinality went from ~1200 hot keys to ~18k. Batching helps throughput but cache hit surface shrank.
sahil: the intention was to avoid mixing telemetry samples for different eval groups; but we didn't budget the cache implications.
maria: reproducer: load dashboard with 6 widgets, canary -> open devtools Performance. Timeline: long task at t+0.78s and chart paints delayed. console client logs show `kvcache.miss` for the tile requests.
jon: we should rollback the samplingGroupId suffix in the key while we design a better sharding strategy. Can we do a quick revert in canary?
sahil: deploy-bot shows the canary rollout is 12% traffic. I can cut it back to 0% in ~2m if we want. Thoughts?
alex: do it. Also open a short-term mitigation: switch samplingGroupId to only be appended when samplingGroupId != "default" (rare) — that'll preserve most cache locality.
samir: agree. fallback plan: if miss rate > 40% for 5m, revert automatically.
maria: +1 to tapering canary and quick patch. I'll open an incident ticket and add perf traces.
jon: action items: sahil — cut canary to 0%, samir — prepare a 2-line client patch (conditional suffix), maria — collect perf trace link and graphs, alex — add a kvcache alarm to avoid >50% miss for 10m.
sahil: starting canary rollback now (cutting 12% -> 0%). deploy-bot: canary rollback completed at 1748002450, version telemetry-batcher-v2 -> telemetry-batcher-v1.
deploy-bot: deploy log: roll back telemetry-batcher-v2 canary -> v1 ; duration 90s ; triggered by sahil
maria: post-rollback quick check: miss rate down to 14% after ~2m, avg paint back to baseline.
jon: great. please still follow up with a proper design doc for how we want sampling isolation without destroying kvcache reuse.
samir: I'll draft the doc with options: metadata sharding, LRU per-group buckets, or separate ephemeral cache keyed by samplingGroupId but with shared prefixes.
maria: thanks everyone. saving traces/heap snapshots in the incident ticket. we'll coordinate on the doc in #eng-platform tomorrow.
__notes: Document conforms to agents.md: single continuous string of messages, no title field. Root timestamp equals filename timestamp. Kept concise Slack-style messages and included code snippet and deploy-bot lines.
